content.value_statement: Skill documentation often needs localized versions for international users. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code translate SKILL.md and README.md while preserving technical text.
actual_capabilities: Translates SKILL.md and README.md documentation into selected languages.
Creates language-specific files with consistent naming conventions.
Preserves code blocks, file paths, command names, URLs, and identifiers.
Stores default languages, target files, and per-skill settings.
Supports non-interactive flags for automated documentation workflows.
limitations: The skill contains guidance, not a standalone executable translator.
Translation quality still depends on the model and user review.
It focuses on skill documentation, not application UI strings.
It uses local configuration paths under the Claude skills directory.

use_cases.title: Publish localized skill docs
use_cases.description: Create translated skill documentation before sharing a skill with international users.

use_cases.title: Keep translations aligned
use_cases.description: Regenerate localized documentation when the source SKILL.md or README.md changes.

use_cases.title: Add translation to workflows
use_cases.description: Use non-interactive settings to include documentation translation in release or publishing workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Translate current skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup in the current directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate the SKILL.md file in the current skill directory to the configured languages.

prompt_templates.title: Translate selected files
prompt_templates.scenario: Translate more than one documentation file
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate both SKILL.md and README.md for this skill into Chinese and Japanese.

prompt_templates.title: Configure defaults
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure default translation languages for new skills, then save the settings for future runs.

prompt_templates.title: Automate a named skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a non-interactive translation workflow for a named skill and skip prompts when settings are supplied.

output_examples.input: A skill author asks for Chinese and Japanese versions of a skill document.
output: Creates Simplified Chinese and Japanese documentation files.
Keeps commands, file paths, and code examples unchanged.
Reports which translated files were produced.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks to update existing translations after changing the source document.
output: Detects existing translated files before replacement.
Offers overwrite, skip, or individual selection choices.
Updates only the selected localized documentation files.

output_examples.input: An automation workflow requests translation without interactive prompts.
output: Uses supplied language and file settings.
Generates translated documentation for the named skill.
Saves configuration for future translation runs.

best_practices: Review translated files before publishing them to users.
Set default languages before translating many skills.
Keep code blocks and command names unchanged in every translation.
anti_patterns: Translating code blocks or file paths as normal prose.
Overwriting existing translations without checking local changes.
Using this skill for product UI localization without extra context.

faq.question: Which languages are shown in the skill?
faq.answer: The examples cover Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, and custom language codes.

faq.question: Does it translate code examples?
faq.answer: No. It preserves code blocks, file paths, command names, URLs, and technical identifiers.

faq.question: Can it translate README files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can translate SKILL.md, README.md, or both when those files are selected.

faq.question: Where are preferences stored?
faq.answer: Preferences are stored in a local skill-specific configuration file under the Claude directory.

faq.question: Can it run without prompts?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports supplied language and file settings for non-interactive workflows.

faq.question: Should translations be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review localized files for accuracy, tone, and preserved technical text before publishing.
